title: Two incomplete suits, no side support
author_notes: EC-055 checkpoint-3 coverage: second Mixed/ambiguous bidding judgment scenario for the checkpoint-3 coverage matrix (see bid_training_009 for the first; both keep primary_skill trump_selection since no dedicated tag exists yet, and are classified as Mixed/ambiguous only in docs/MVP_STATUS.md's coverage matrix). Deliberately different texture from bid_training_009: that hand has controls spread thin across every suit with no length, while this hand has two genuinely comparable four-card trump candidates (King-Queen of Spades vs. Ace-Jack of Hearts) and no help anywhere else — Diamonds and Clubs are entirely low. Neither candidate is clearly better than the other, and unlike bid_training_006-010's trump_selection pairs, no side-suit Ace or King outside the two candidates breaks the tie. No evaluation in this scenario reaches Strong. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: One defensible choice among two close options
feedback.summary: King-Queen of Spades gives two trump honors and enough length to compete, but Ace-Jack of Hearts is a comparable alternative from the same hand.
points: Control: King-Queen of Spades are two trump honors; four cards is adequate but not commanding length.
Neither Diamonds nor Clubs offers a side honor to support this or any other choice.
Choosing Hearts instead is equally defensible here; this is a genuine judgment call, not a clearly correct answer.

feedback.title: One defensible choice among two close options
feedback.summary: The Ace of Hearts is a genuine trump control card, and the Jack gives a second honor, but King-Queen of Spades is a comparable alternative from the same hand.
points: Control: the Ace of Hearts is the single highest card in either candidate suit; the Jack adds a second honor.
Neither Diamonds nor Clubs offers a side honor to support this or any other choice.
Choosing Spades instead is equally defensible here; this is a genuine judgment call, not a clearly correct answer.

feedback.title: A fifth trick has no clear source
feedback.summary: King-Queen of Spades supports a cautious target; a fifth trick needs a low Spade promoted or a card from a suit with no honors at all.
points: Two trump honors and moderate length do not by themselves establish a fifth trick.
Diamonds and Clubs hold nothing higher than a nine, so neither can be counted on for an extra winner.
This is not unreasonable, but it stretches past what either candidate suit visibly supports.

feedback.title: A fifth trick has no clear source
feedback.summary: The Ace and Jack of Hearts support a cautious target; a fifth trick needs a low Heart promoted or a card from a suit with no honors at all.
points: One certain trump winner and one further honor do not by themselves establish a fifth trick.
Diamonds and Clubs hold nothing higher than a nine, so neither can be counted on for an extra winner.
This is not unreasonable, but it stretches past what either candidate suit visibly supports.
